statement: In fictional test system four, lowering setting X with agent Q raises counter Y.
rationale: Agent Q acts on fictional target T, which limits counter Y.
benefit: If true, operators of system four could keep counter Y high for longer.
prior_work: Fictional study F1 linked target T to counter Y; agent Q has not been tested.
open_question: Does target T limit counter Y in fictional system five as well?
alternative: Agent Q may raise counter Y through fictional target U instead of T.
base_rate: Of 40 fictional agents screened in system four, 6 raised counter Y.
replication: Study F1 was repeated once by an independent fictional group, with the same result.
funding: Study F1 was funded by fictional fund G. The authors declare no competing interests.
dataset: Fictional dataset D4 records counter Y for 200 runs of system four with and without agent Q.
cost: A test run needs about two weeks and one fictional bench, costing 1000 to 1500 EUR in 2026.
resolution: The prediction holds if counter Y is at least 10 percent higher with agent Q after 20 cycles.
human: The fictional system four has no human counterpart; no human study applies.
heuristic: We compared competing explanations for the rise in counter Y.
